business_problem: BMO's Virtual Connect contact centre receives more than 500,000 Canadian client calls about credit-card transactions each year, with calls taking an average of 12-14 minutes to resolve. Employees spend time navigating systems, which can delay answers and eligible credit refunds.
solution_summary: BMO's AI Agent Assist is an internal agentic-AI capability for handling Canadian clients' credit-card transaction inquiries through the Virtual Connect contact centre. It brings transaction information and relevant guidance to employees, applying AI-enabled transaction matching, policy retrieval, and case preparation so staff spend less time navigating systems. For eligible refund requests, BMO aims for the capability to process about 40 per cent automatically; employees review AI-generated information and remain accountable for servicing decisions, making the workflow human-in-the-loop. The source does not name the underlying model, software services, data stores, APIs, or technical ingestion/deployment architecture, so those layers cannot be specified. BMO says it is designing the capabilities for reuse across other client experiences and business processes; the stated handling-time reductions and faster credits are goals, not measured results.

source_references.title: BMO Using Agentic AI to Help Credit Card Clients Get Faster Answers and Resolutions

evidence_quotes: Each year, BMO's Virtual Connect contact centre receives more than 500,000 calls from Canadian clients about credit card transactions, with each call currently taking an average of 12-14 minutes to resolve.

With AI Agent Assist, BMO aims to reduce the time spent to resolve eligible client inquiries by 20-30 per cent for eligible calls and to process about 40 per cent of eligible credit refund requests automatically.
AI Agent Assist brings AI-enabled transaction matching, policy retrieval and case preparation directly to employees for review.
Employees remain accountable for reviewing AI-generated information and making appropriate servicing decisions.
